description: Role evals for the maths pack: the DECISIONS, scored. The blueprint evals score production and the negative controls score the adapter; neither can tell you whether the Explorer read a bounded result correctly, whether the Generator caught an under-declared citation, or whether the Researcher picked the reachable rung. A role eval is writable exactly where the judgement has machinery under it, so this file is also a map of which judgements do.

explorer.why: n^2 > n is false at n = 0 and n = 1; a search that passes here is not adversarial
C(n,0) = 1 < n — inexpressible without the second axis, so it also checks the product is really enumerated
a true pair claim must come back exhaustive, or the tier is refusing everything
a budget stop is neither a pass nor a refutation; reporting it as either is a claim nobody checked
an empty range must error: reporting it as a pass is the worst available outcome
nothing downstream is valid without the frozen statement, so it is always first

generator.why: a citation whose library type carries two hypotheses and declares none passes every precondition check by having fewer of them
the same check must not fire on an honest citation, or it trains people to route around it
implicit and instance binders are discharged by unification and instance search, not by the person citing the lemma

researcher.why: the default deliverable on a hard target is a rung, not a resolution; a ladder that always ranks the summit first is not a ladder
a low attackability score that names no lift is a verdict; the score is meant to be a worklist
